correctness.rationale: For N=2d there is precisely one angular DFT alias, at ±d, whose two radial-normalized real projections have determinant minus sin(d delta). When nonsingular the data determine both continuous circle squared magnitudes; the rational quotient is dilation-invariant and therefore a unimodular constant. When singular the explicit pair 1±i z^d collides. The exact B-transpose-B trace/determinant formula gives singular values sqrt(1±abs(cos(d delta))). A fresh standalone standard-library checker passed 9639 deterministic finite arithmetic assertions; proofs are independent of the finite tests.
